title: Iran-Aligned 'Islamic Resistance in Iraq' Postpones Retaliation Against US-Saudi Strikes After Badr Mediation
detail: The Islamic Resistance in Iraq — a coalition of Iran-backed Iraqi militias — had set a deadline of 23 Safar (around August 7, 2026) for the federal government to respond to joint US-Saudi airstrikes the previous week on Iran-aligned militia positions inside Iraq, threatening retaliation against US assets and Saudi Arabia if Baghdad failed to act, with a senior Saudi official warning the planned attacks could target civilian and economic infrastructure. On August 7, the coalition announced it would postpone its response after mediation by Badr Organization leader Hadi al-Amiri, who urged fighters to 'postpone any reaction to the American-Saudi aggression and to bite the wound for the greater good of Iraq.' Iraqi security forces were placed on high alert as the deadline expired. The episode underscored the fragility of the ceasefire dynamic even as Baghdad presses factions toward the September 30 disarmament deadline.

media.caption: Iraqi security forces on high alert as an Iran-aligned militia deadline for retaliation against US-Saudi strikes expires
